newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly higher on Thursday mainly due to a new domestic A share issue on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 11.20 percent from 9.98 percent on Wednesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market soared to 8.4 million lots from 2.9 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said Beijing Wandong Medicine Company's new issue of A shares on Thursday, and two other new issues scheduled for Friday boosted fund demand on the repo market and pushed up repo rates.
"Institutional buying was seen especially in early-maturing contracts," said one trader. "They borrowed heavily to mobilise funds to bid for the new shares."
Volume was much larger than Wednesday because of the increased demand for funds, traders said.
They said they expect most contracts to stay around the current level on Friday, but the three-day contract will likely fall.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed on Thursday with some contracts being hit by profit-taking after rises the past few days, traders said.
The most actively traded three-year bond, which matures in August, 1999, fell slightly to 107.72 yuan from 107.77 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market rose slightly to 1.05 million lots from 1.02 million lots.

Traders said activity will continue to be slow due to market uncertainties after Beijing last week announced the set-up of a national state debt depository. Spot prices are likely to move narrowly in the short term due to the uncertainty.
